title: Charge-monitored Luttinger liquid
abstract: We discuss phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids without particle number conservation, such as those in proximity to a superconductor, subjected to weak continuous measurements of their particle density, in the regime where the bosonization approach is applicable. We show that the phases of these systems are controlled by the competition between measurements, which favor the area-law phase and particle tunneling in and out of the Luttinger liquid, which favors the volume-law phase. The volume-law phase in this system is always charge fuzzy. We show that within this framework, the phase boundary between the two phases is given by a universal dependence of the Luttinger parameter on the measurement rate. This behavior can be contrasted with the non-universal phase boundaries in more generic highly excited one dimensional systems whose behavior is no longer captured by the Luttinger liquid framework.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how continuous quantum measurements affect the ground state phases of one-dimensional interacting fermions (Luttinger liquids). By using advanced field theory techniques, the authors map out a phase diagram governed by the competition between measurement back-action and intrinsic particle tunneling. This reveals a universal phase transition boundary that distinguishes between charge-sharp and charge-fuzzy steady states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-equilibrium phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids subjected to weak, continuous measurements of their particle density.
main_result: The system exhibits a phase transition controlled by the competition between measurement-induced charge sharpening (area-law) and particle tunneling fluctuations (volume-law), with the boundary depending universally on the Luttinger parameter.
method: The analysis employs the bosonization approach combined with the Keldysh functional integral formalism to handle non-unitary evolution induced by measurements.
model_or_system: The model is an interacting fermionic Luttinger liquid (1D system) whose dynamics are modified by weak continuous measurements of particle density, analyzed using replica techniques.

important_parameters: Luttinger parameter ($K$), dimensionless measurement rate ($\hat{\lambda}$), and the replica number ($R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the low-energy regime where the bosonization approach is valid, and initial calculations rely on quadratic action approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the phase diagram in the $K-\hat{\lambda}$ plane, showing the boundary separating the volume-law charge-fuzzy and the area-law charge-sharp phases.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the full action incorporating measurement terms, calculating scaling dimensions for $	heta$ and $\phi$ fields in real space-time, and finally mapping the competition between these terms to define the phase boundary.
why_interesting: The use of Keldysh formalism and replica techniques to study non-equilibrium steady states driven by measurement is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum measurement theory.
